name: matches an independent symmetric cross-entropy reference
test:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
torch.manual_seed(11)
images=torch.randn(4,5,dtype=torch.double,requires_grad=True)
texts=torch.randn(4,5,dtype=torch.double,requires_grad=True)
actual=clip_contrastive_loss(images,texts,temperature=.2)
i=images/images.norm(dim=1,keepdim=True); t=texts/texts.norm(dim=1,keepdim=True)
logits=i@t.T/.2; labels=torch.arange(4)
expected=(F.cross_entropy(logits,labels)+F.cross_entropy(logits.T,labels))/2
torch.testing.assert_close(actual,expected,rtol=1e-4,atol=1e-5)
ga=torch.autograd.grad(actual,(images,texts)); ge=torch.autograd.grad(expected,(images,texts))
for got,want in zip(ga,ge): torch.testing.assert_close(got,want,rtol=1e-4,atol=1e-5)
print('ok')

name: supports raw dot products and a singleton batch
input: normalize false and batch size one
test:
import torch
images=torch.tensor([[1.,2.],[3.,4.]])
texts=torch.tensor([[2.,0.],[0.,1.]])
snapshot=(images.clone(),texts.clone())
loss=clip_contrastive_loss(images,texts,temperature=2.,normalize=False)
logits=images@texts.T/2; labels=torch.arange(2)
expected=(torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits,labels)+torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits.T,labels))/2
torch.testing.assert_close(loss,expected)
assert torch.equal(images,snapshot[0]) and torch.equal(texts,snapshot[1])
assert clip_contrastive_loss(torch.ones(1,3),torch.ones(1,3)).item()==0
print('ok')

name: asymmetric retrieval averages both directions and keeps diagonal targets
input: distinct row/column losses; paired and text-only permutations
test:
import torch
images = torch.eye(3)
texts = torch.tensor([[5., 0., -2.], [4., 5., 1.], [-1., 2., 3.]])
def expected_loss(images, texts):
    logits = images @ texts.T / 2.
    diagonal = logits.diagonal()
    row_loss = (logits.logsumexp(dim=1) - diagonal).mean()
    column_loss = (logits.logsumexp(dim=0) - diagonal).mean()
    return (row_loss + column_loss) / 2, row_loss, column_loss
expected, row_loss, column_loss = expected_loss(images, texts)
assert abs((row_loss - column_loss).item()) > .01
actual = clip_contrastive_loss(images, texts, temperature=2., normalize=False)
torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5)
order = torch.tensor([2, 0, 1])
paired = clip_contrastive_loss(images[order], texts[order], 2., False)
torch.testing.assert_close(paired, expected, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5)
reordered = clip_contrastive_loss(images, texts[order], 2., False)
reordered_expected, _, _ = expected_loss(images, texts[order])
torch.testing.assert_close(reordered, reordered_expected, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5)
assert abs((reordered_expected - expected).item()) > .1
print('ok')

name: row normalization ignores positive scales and tied candidates give log batch size
input: independent row scales; identical nonzero embeddings; normalized input preservation
test:
import math
import torch
images = torch.tensor([[1., -2., 3.], [-3., 1., 2.], [2., 4., -1.]])
texts = torch.tensor([[3., -1., 1.], [-2., 3., 1.], [1., 2., -4.]])
snapshots = [images.clone(), texts.clone()]
baseline = clip_contrastive_loss(images, texts, .3)
scaled = clip_contrastive_loss(images * torch.tensor([[.1], [7.], [30.]]),
                               texts * torch.tensor([[11.], [.2], [4.]]), .3)
torch.testing.assert_close(scaled, baseline, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5)
for tensor, snapshot in zip((images, texts), snapshots):
    assert torch.equal(tensor, snapshot), 'Do not normalize inputs in place'
tied_images = torch.tensor([[1., -2., 3.]]).repeat(4, 1)
tied_texts = torch.tensor([[-1., 2., 1.]]).repeat(4, 1)
for normalize in (True, False):
    loss = clip_contrastive_loss(tied_images, tied_texts, .3, normalize)
    torch.testing.assert_close(loss, torch.tensor(math.log(4)), rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5)
print('ok')

name: noncontiguous embeddings preserve scalar dtype and gradients in both modes
input: CPU float32/float64; transposed inputs; normalized and raw gradients
test:
import torch
torch.manual_seed(408)
for dtype in (torch.float32, torch.float64):
    for normalize in (True, False):
        images = torch.randn(5, 3, dtype=dtype).T.requires_grad_()
        texts = torch.randn(5, 3, dtype=dtype).T.requires_grad_()
        assert not images.is_contiguous() and not texts.is_contiguous()
        snapshots = [images.clone(), texts.clone()]
        actual = clip_contrastive_loss(images, texts, .7, normalize)
        assert actual.ndim == 0
        assert actual.dtype == dtype and actual.device == images.device
        i, t = images, texts
        if normalize:
            i = images / images.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
            t = texts / texts.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        logits = i @ t.T / .7
        expected = ((logits.logsumexp(dim=1) - logits.diagonal()).mean()
                    + (logits.logsumexp(dim=0) - logits.diagonal()).mean()) / 2
        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5)
        actual_grads = torch.autograd.grad(actual, (images, texts))
        expected_grads = torch.autograd.grad(expected, (images, texts))
        for got, want in zip(actual_grads, expected_grads):
            assert torch.isfinite(got).all() and got.abs().sum() > 0
            torch.testing.assert_close(got, want, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5)
        for tensor, snapshot in zip((images, texts), snapshots):
            assert torch.equal(tensor, snapshot)
print('ok')

name: temperature extremes stay finite without explicitly logging softmax probabilities
input: small positive temperature, confident wrong matches, and large-temperature uniform limit
test:
import math
import torch
images = torch.eye(2, requires_grad=True)
texts = torch.tensor([[0., 1.], [1., 0.]], requires_grad=True)
for normalize in (True, False):
    loss = clip_contrastive_loss(images, texts, temperature=1e-4, normalize=normalize)
    assert torch.isfinite(loss)
    torch.testing.assert_close(loss, torch.tensor(10000.), rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5)
    grads = torch.autograd.grad(loss, (images, texts))
    assert all(torch.isfinite(g).all() and g.abs().sum() > 0 for g in grads)
    matched = clip_contrastive_loss(images, images, temperature=1e-4, normalize=normalize)
    torch.testing.assert_close(matched, torch.tensor(0.), rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5)
    flat = clip_contrastive_loss(images, texts, temperature=1e6, normalize=normalize)
    torch.testing.assert_close(flat, torch.tensor(math.log(2)), rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5)
print('ok')
